main_issue: Whether and how strong-smelling cooking (e.g. D's salted fish) can continue in the shared flat; the group settles on containment measures plus cooking after 7pm or on Saturdays, with D warning B beforehand.

A-B.evidence: B agrees with A's complaint (T2). B says containment still leaves smell (T14) and A backs B (T17). B accepts the warning arrangement (T18, T21), and A closes with 'that's what we'll do' (T26).

A-C.evidence: C also complains about smelly laundry (T5) and says closing the yard door works (T15). A's package includes that door closure (T13, T17).

A-D.evidence: A first asks for no strong-smelling food (T1) and D resists (T6, T8). A then offers containment and an after-7pm or Saturday window (T9, T13, T17), and D agrees 'After 7pm is fine' (T22).

B-C.evidence: B and C reinforce each other on the laundry (T10, T11). C then accepts the door closure (T15) while B wants more, so they are aligned but not identical.

B-D.evidence: D resists the complaints (T6, T8, T12). D then agrees to tell B before cooking (T20) and B says 'That works' (T21).

C-D.evidence: C complains about the laundry smell (T5). D accepts the closed yard door (T16), which is the measure C said works (T15).
